To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The activity of brain Na,K-ATPase is significantly reduced in vivo in rats in the deep stages of galactosamine induced liver failure.
the brain Na+, K+ ATPase enzyme is inhibited in vivo by circulating substances in rats with galatosamine induced liver failure.
the activity of Na+,K+-ATPase in the brain was reduced in rats with galatcosamine-induced hepatic coma and this was associated with a reduced ability of the brain to pump out excess sodium ions.

the pathogenesis of hepatic encephalopathy.
the possible pathogenesis of hepatic coma.
the pathogenesis of cerebral oedemaa and encephalopathy in fulminant hepatis failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a significant decrease in the activity of the Na+, K+-dependent ATPase in the brain during the development of hepatic encephalopathy in rats.
there is a decrease in brain Na+,K+-ATPase which may be involved in both the pathogenesis of coma and cerebral oedemata in rats with D-Galactosamine-induced fulminant hepate failure.

the activity of brain sodium-potassium-adenosine triphosphatase is reduced in vivo in rats in the later stages of hepatic failure and that this is associated with the development of encephalpathy and cerebral oedemata.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reduction of brain Na+,K+-ATPase may contribute to the pathogenesis of cerebral oedemata and encephalopathy in rats and patients with fulminan hepatic failure.

the inhibition of Na+, K+ ATPase activity in the brain of rats with galactoasamine-induced hepatic encephalopathy may contribute to the development of coma, but not to cerebral oedema, in these animals.
the inhibition of Na+,K+-ATPase by serum from rats with galactoseamine induced hepatic coma is a consequence of the hepatic failure and that this inhibition is associated with coma.

we have found that a reduction in brain Na+K-ATPase is an early and consistent feature of hepatic encephalopathy in rats with D-Galactosamine-induced liver failure.
we have identified a novel therapeutic target for the treatment of hepatic encephalopathy.
